name: Sliding genioplasty
lead: Sliding genioplasty is a chin surgery in which a surgeon cuts the lower part of the chin bone and moves it forward, backward, vertically or sideways, then fixes it in place [1][2]. Unlike an implant, it uses the patient's own bone.

It is used for cosmetic chin reshaping, in facial feminization, and as part of face-contouring and jaw surgery [3][4][5]. On looksmaxxing forums it is discussed as a hardmaxxing option, often compared with chin implants [6].
infobox: Oral and maxillofacial or plastic surgeons
Titanium plate and screws, or wires

paras: Wikipedia describes cutting a horseshoe-shaped piece of the lower jaw border and repositioning it, held with a titanium step plate and screws; it may be combined with rhinoplasty [1]. A paper on feminization states sliding genioplasty has the most potential for dramatic reshaping while avoiding implant issues, and that the mental nerve can be protected during surgery [3].

Uses documented in the literature include facial feminization [3], contouring a square jaw in East Asian patients combined with mandibular surgery [4][7], and balancing facial aesthetics [8]. Genioplasty does not correct bite; a significant overbite may need orthognathic surgery [1].

Reported effects include swelling, hematoma, and temporary lip weakness or numbness; less common are infection, displacement and nerve damage [1]. A 1996 paper addressed avoiding mental nerve injuries [9].

A systematic review looked at soft-to-hard tissue ratios in chin procedures including sliding genioplasty [10]. A ten-year surgeon experience series described sliding osteotomy for aesthetic balance [8]. A registered trial compared fat or PEEK onlay augmentation with sliding genioplasty for deficient chin in 12 patients [11]. A study assessed YouTube videos on genioplasty as a source of information [12]. Wikipedia says its sources are mainly case series and reviews and lack comparative trial data [1].

Users on looksmax.org ask whether a genioplasty would widen or advance a chin, whether to choose it over an implant, and how to evaluate outcomes such as asymmetry after surgery [6][13][14]. One poster reported a surgeon advising typical advancements of 6 to 7 mm [13]. Surgeons quoted by posters have also said swelling can look asymmetric early on [14].

timeline.event: Aufricht's work on combined nose and chin surgery is cited in the literature [1].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, sliding genioplasty is discussed as a way to improve profile or chin width, often weighed against implants or jaw surgery [6][13].

claims.claim: Sliding genioplasty can widen a narrow chin
claims.believers: A poster relayed that his surgeon said an osteotomy could make the chin wider and more masculine [13].
claims.experts: Literature describes sliding genioplasty as able to move the chin in multiple dimensions [3]; published trials of widening for appearance were not found.

claims.claim: Genioplasty can compensate for a poor bite or weak jaw
claims.believers: Posters ask whether it can substitute for bimaxillary surgery [15].
claims.experts: Wikipedia states genioplasty does not correct bite and orthognathic surgery may be needed [1].

card.summary: Cutting and moving the chin bone to reshape the chin; established surgery with case-series evidence and few comparative trials.
card.note: Reported effects include swelling and temporary lip numbness; nerve injury is rarer.

quick.overview:
Sliding genioplasty cuts the lower chin bone and repositions it, then fixes it with plates. It is used for chin projection, reduction, and feminization.

Evidence is mostly case series and reviews.
quick.mechanism: The cut bone segment moves to a new position and is fixed with plate and screws, altering chin shape using the patient's own bone.
quick.risks: Swelling, temporary numbness, infection, displacement and nerve damage have been reported; it does not correct bite.
